2607.27547.title: AI Literacy: An Exercise in Power-Knowledge
2607.27547.paper_summary: As generative artificial intelligence becomes one of the most significant systems of knowledge production in our society today, questions relating to who can access and shape that production grow increasingly important in our discourse. This paper argues that the existing frameworks for AI literacy, which are dominated by technical competency and responsible-use principles, are insufficient because they enforce a "consumer" orientation toward AI rather than fostering genuine epistemic agency. Based upon Foucault's concept of power-knowledge, Freire's pedagogy of critical consciousness, and scholarship of digital literacy, this paper proposes a reconceptualization of AI literacy as a critical practice that equips individuals not just to use AI systems, but to critically evaluate them, resist their structuring assumptions, and participate in their governance. The paper further argues that unequal access to AI tools in society recapitulates longstanding epistemic injustices, and that a literacy framework oriented toward empowerment must account for these structural inequities. A three-part framework of AI literacy based on the notions of contextual use, critical interrogation, and participatory governance frames this literacy as a cultivation of epistemic "agents" rather than the training of competent consumers of AI-generated information.
2607.27547.paper_summary_zh: 隨著生成性人工智慧成為我們當今社會中最重要的知識生產系統之一，關於誰能夠訪問和塑造這種生產的問題在我們的討論中變得越來越重要。本文主張，現有的人工智慧素養框架，主要以技術能力和負責任使用原則為主，並不足夠，因為它們強化了對人工智慧的「消費者」導向，而非促進真正的認識主體性。基於福柯的權力-知識概念、弗雷雷的批判意識教育學以及數位素養的學術研究，本文提出將人工智慧素養重新概念化為一種批判性實踐，使個體不僅能夠使用人工智慧系統，還能夠批判性地評估它們、抵抗其結構性假設，並參與其治理。本文進一步主張，社會中對人工智慧工具的不平等訪問重申了長期存在的認識不公，而一個以賦權為導向的素養框架必須考慮這些結構性不平等。基於情境使用、批判性質疑和參與式治理的三部分人工智慧素養框架，將這種素養視為對認識「主體」的培養，而非對人工智慧生成信息的合格消費者的培訓。
